public_rationale: The claim says GitHub Copilot was losing money around the time it had about 1.8 million paid users. The contract sets the period as October 2024 to February 2025. The speaker relies on a Wall Street Journal report from October 2023. That report cited an anonymous source and said GitHub lost up to $80 per user per month earlier in 2023. GitHub denied those figures (e2). In November 2023, GitHub's CEO said the cost to run Copilot per user was lower than the price. He also described the product's margins as 'growing positive' (e1). Both sources are from 2023, before the target period, and they conflict. Neither cited item reports Copilot's revenue against its costs for October 2024 to February 2025. So the evidence in the case cannot confirm or refute the claim for that period.
limitations: No evidence item covers Copilot's revenue or costs for October 2024 to February 2025.
The evidence includes no Microsoft or GitHub breakdown of Copilot revenue or costs.
The CEO's margin claim (e1) is an unaudited company statement and covers per-user running costs, not fully loaded profit or loss.
The WSJ loss figures (e2) rest on one anonymous source, were denied by the company, and concern early 2023.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: around the time GitHub Copilot had about 1.8 million paid subscribers (late 2024) and up to the post, the product's costs exceeded its revenue. That is, it was loss-making on a product basis, including on paying users.
The 1.8 million figure is background, not the claim being tested.
Target period: October 2024 to February 2025, from the 1.8 million figure 'a year later' than October 2023 up to the post. The claim is in the present tense with no period named.
criteria.support_condition: Credible reporting or disclosure that GitHub Copilot's costs (serving costs, at least) exceeded its revenue during October 2024 to February 2025.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible reporting or disclosure that GitHub Copilot had positive margins (revenue above serving costs) during October 2024 to February 2025.
